meta.title: The Other Channel
meta.subtitle: An RPC is an entity that becomes bits on the reliable pipeline, and an entity again on the far side

views.label: Raising one is a spawn
views.note: You do not call anything. You create an entity with two components and let a generated system find it.

views.label: Many RPCs, one packet
views.note: The queue is a byte buffer. The sender fills a packet with as many whole messages as fit.

views.label: Two pipelines, one socket
views.note: Reliable ordered for RPCs. Unreliable drop-old for snapshots and commands. Same connection.

views.label: It becomes an entity again
views.note: The receiver spawns an entity carrying your component plus the connection that sent it.

messages.label: target connection, or null to broadcast
index, bit length, payload → outgoing buffer
one packet, five byte header, whole messages only
send queue full: keep it, retry next tick
snapshots and commands: newest wins, never resent
bits read must equal bits declared

cards.title: The whole API is two components
items: Create an entity carrying your command plus a send request to send one
The send request names one connection, or nothing at all to broadcast
On the far side an entity appears carrying your command plus a receive request
The receive request names the connection it came from, which is your only sender identity

cards.title: Reliable next to unreliable
items: Remote calls take the reliable ordered pipeline: acked, retransmitted, delivered in send order
Snapshots and commands take the unreliable one: newest wins, losses are never made up
Both are the same connection and the same socket, just different pipeline stages
So the ordering guarantee holds within remote calls and nowhere across the two

cards.title: The failure modes are quiet
items: The reliable window can fill, and then sending simply retries on later ticks
A message too large for one packet is a hard error, because it can never be split
A received entity you never consume just sits there, and the age warning is your only clue
Deserializing fewer bits than were declared disconnects the offender on the spot

cards.title: Ordering, precisely
items: Remote calls arrive in the order they were serialised, not the order you raised the entities
Nothing is guaranteed about a remote call relative to a snapshot
So never use one to announce a state change the snapshot also carries
Before approval only the approval kind is accepted, and anything else drops the connection
